decision: Adopt a bounded, staged plan for actual NetMamba+ fine-tuning, saved-classifier inference and the customer package due 15 September 2026. Begin with a GB10 viability pilot, select the execution route by 12 September, and freeze reviewed measured artifacts by 14 September, using America/Los_Angeles dates. Current evidence supports the offline harness, documented source checks, native-data validation and parser dry runs. GPU execution and expanded scientific or deployment claims require the acceptance evidence below. This verification decision does not certify completed experiments or replace the earlier ESCALATED/UNRATIFIED audit.

findings.summary: GB10 compatibility remains unverified. Driver-visible CUDA 13.0 does not establish a usable Torch/custom-kernel stack. The bundled Mamba fork has interfaces absent from stock Mamba 1.1.1; matching package versions or Python sources alone cannot validate compiled kernels.

The supplied evidence confirms a paper-versus-launcher fine-tuning batch difference, 64 versus 128, and batch-scaled learning rates. Complete schedule provenance remains unavailable in the excerpt. A shortened demonstration schedule must be distinguished from both source and paper settings.

findings.summary: Treat fuse3_mamba.pth as pretrained-transfer input, not a ready classifier. Confirm that role through focused source inspection, verify backbone transfer, and strictly reload the subsequently fine-tuned classifier with its recorded class mapping. The evaluator uses weights_only=False; strict state-dictionary loading does not mitigate pickle execution risk.

findings.summary: NPU and SmartNIC targets are unspecified, redistribution rights are not established by this repository, and portions of implementation evidence remain excluded. This focused decision supplies neither device-feasibility clearance nor a replacement full-repository audit.

reasons: The available evidence supports a concrete bounded experiment without expanding current claims prematurely: 43 offline tests, documented upstream integrity, native-flow validation and parser dry runs.
The GB10 route uses the available host and can provide directly relevant execution evidence, but runtime or kernel adaptations must be labeled a compatibility-port experiment.
An already accessible GPU supporting the authors’ pinned stack reduces environment divergence. Its availability and successful pilot must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

A fork-equivalent reference-operation CPU/GPU route can avoid custom-extension obstacles, but requires semantic verification and sufficient measured throughput. It cannot establish native-kernel performance.

Prioritizing fine-tuning and fresh-process inference gives the strongest achievable demonstration. If training cannot complete, publish the honestly scoped partial package and explicitly mark the training requirement unmet; preserve all failed-run evidence and the earlier ESCALATED/UNRATIFIED record.
verify: Before accepting experiment results, inspect the complete, focused configuration, pretrained-weight transfer, native trainer, evaluator and demo paths. Resolve checkpoint-role and automatic-test behavior explicitly. Rerun the full offline suite, currently 43 tests, after relevant changes and add only necessary behavioral or numerical checks. Record commands and outcomes without claiming a new full-repository audit.

By 12 September, select a route using successful native-flow forward/backward execution and measured throughput sufficient to estimate the proposed training and evaluation duration. Probes use training/validation data only. Record failures and the selected route. Prefer the authors’ stack on an already accessible compatible GPU when it passes the pilot and fits the deadline; otherwise use a validated GB10 compatibility port or a validated reference-operation route.

Preserve upstream commit eec9483e2f0fb84ca22982b9de8149bc3a8b1ad2 unchanged and record modifications separately. Capture source and patch hashes, installed fork identity, dependency/build lock, Python/Torch versions, actual CUDA runtime, driver, compiler, architecture flags and build commands. For the native-extension route, force the bundled source build and compare installed Python sources with the intended bundled-plus-patch sources. Patched or substituted operations must pass forward and gradient comparisons against references preserving the fork’s semantics, using declared precision-specific tolerances; source matching alone does not pass this gate.

Each run records code, configuration, split-file, checkpoint and class-map hashes; seed; hardware; precision; resolved arguments; elapsed time; and actual completed optimizer updates. Publish a paper/source/demo settings comparison covering preprocessing, steps versus epochs, batch size, accumulation, world size, learning-rate scaling and schedule. Record effective batch size and effective learning rate, not blr alone. Predeclare shortened schedules and checkpoint-selection rules; prefer the source fine-tuning schedule when the pilot supports completion.

Verify the cached pretrained checkpoint’s trusted origin and hash before loading. Inspect the intended transfer path and record loaded, omitted and newly initialized parameters. Explain expected classifier-head differences and reject unexplained missing backbone weights. Bind the resulting fine-tuned checkpoint to its training run and class-index mapping. Never treat strict=True as protection against untrusted pickle content.

Revalidate the effective data representation and class mapping. For unchanged released files, confirm the documented 8,323 training, 1,040 validation and 1,041 test records and preserve the disclosed overlaps. Restrict engineering probes to training/validation data and smoke pretraining to training data. Suppress automatic final-test execution during exploratory runs. Freeze settings and validation-based checkpoint selection before any final test exposure, and record every test access and any earlier exposure.

Demonstrate genuine supervised fine-tuning through finite losses and gradients, completed optimizer steps, changed trainable parameters and a saved classifier checkpoint. Record learning curves and completion against the declared training budget; optimizer updates alone do not prove convergence. Schedule a bounded downstream pretraining smoke check after protecting the fine-tuning budget, record its completion status separately, and label any success as pretraining-path execution on downstream training data rather than reproduction of the paper’s pretraining corpus or history.

Ensure the permitted final evaluation uses the frozen, validation-selected classifier, accounting for the native trainer’s automatic final-test pass. Strictly reload that classifier in a fresh process with its recorded class mapping and perform actual inference. Re-evaluation may verify the same frozen result; it is not another independent holdout and must not drive further model selection. Retain predictions and confirm agreement under declared deterministic or numerical tolerances.

Independently recompute reported metrics from retained predictions and labels. Check confusion-matrix totals, class supports, accuracy and explicitly named macro/weighted precision, recall and F1 conventions. Report the original released-split result with overlap and unknown pretrained exposure disclosed. Any overlap-excluded sensitivity analysis must be predeclared, preserve the original result, and avoid claims of capture independence. Publish aggregate evidence when per-example records lack sharing clearance.

For speed claims, record hardware, precision, actual input shape, batch size, warm-up, repetition count and latency distribution. Synchronize CUDA measurements and distinguish model execution from preprocessing, transfers and end-to-end inference. Report flows per second without inferring network line rate. Comparative advantages require comparable measured baselines. Paper-reproduction claims require resolved protocol differences and relevant pretraining provenance; IDS generalization requires suitably independent, representative evaluation. NPU/SmartNIC feasibility requires named-device operator, precision, memory and I/O analysis, and device-performance claims require on-target measurements.

Rehearse the demo from a fresh process using the saved fine-tuned classifier and reviewed inputs. Show actual predictions linked to the checkpoint and run evidence, with limitations stated plainly. Provide a clearly labeled recording of a successful measured run as a presentation backup. Checkpoint inspection, prerecorded outputs without an underlying successful run, or direct classifier loading from the pretraining checkpoint cannot satisfy actual training and inference.

By 14 September, build and visually review the PDF, PowerPoint and editable sources. Include a short technical explanation, research citations, reproducible commands, measured results, limitations and a claim-to-run/hash table in the existing GitHub repository. Verify links and intended recipient access. Review publication changes, logs, exports, presentation notes and metadata for secrets, private chat and third-party redistribution rights; link third-party assets unless redistribution is established. Review affected lesson sources and references, recording real content review before updating coverage baselines and leaving unresolved content/video work visible. Verify that the frozen package and rehearsed demo are available for 15 September delivery.
